domain: AI Safety / Technology Governance / Risk Assessment
topic_summary: Analysis of the contested AI-risk kernel: whether AI safety discourse should prioritize existential risks (AGI alignment, humanity-level extinction) or near-term harms (algorithmic bias, labor displacement, surveillance). Each reading interprets the same substrate—'AI poses serious risks requiring governance'—but emits structurally different constraints with distinct victim sets, timescales, and resource allocations.

key_entities: Existential Risk Community (x-risk; focused on AGI catastrophe, alignment research)
Near-Term Harms Community (algorithmic justice; focused on deployed systems, marginalized populations)
AI Safety Research Institutions (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind safety teams)
AI Ethics/Fairness Research Community (ACM FAccT, Data & Society)
Regulatory Bodies (EU AI Act, U.S. NTIA, proposed governance frameworks)
key_tensions: Resource Allocation: x-risk research funding vs algorithmic justice intervention funding
Epistemic Authority: who defines 'serious AI risk'—technical AI researchers or social scientists/affected communities

omegas.description: Do the two readings share a common substrate, or are they two distinct kernels? X-risk reading treats AI as potential agentic catastrophe (alignment problem); near-term reading treats AI as instantiation of existing power structures (fairness problem). They may share the word 'AI risk' but reference structurally different phenomena. If so, 'AI risk' is a homonym covering two kernels, not one contested kernel.

Can a single coherent framework hold both 'AGI alignment is paramount' AND 'deployed-system justice is paramount'? If yes, they are complementary rather than axiom-contradictory. If no (zero-sum resource allocation, mutually exclusive victim prioritization), they are axiom-contradictory. Current evidence suggests resource zero-sum but not necessarily axiom contradiction—may be licensed plurality rather than mutual exclusion.

Is the kernel contest itself downstream of ML capability progress rate? If capabilities plateau below AGI, x-risk reading collapses; if capabilities accelerate to superintelligence, near-term reading appears retrospectively negligent. The readings may be time-indexed rather than axiom-contradictory.

Both selected readings treat AI as risk object. A third reading: 'AI risk discourse is itself a capital accumulation mechanism—both x-risk and fairness frames serve to legitimize AI deployment while capturing regulatory/funding resources.' This reading would treat the kernel as snare rather than mountain. Deferred for token budget but may be the structurally central reading.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition successfully identifies two structurally distinct readings with different victim sets and resource allocations. Omega_kernel_coherence flags uncertainty about whether this is one contested kernel or two distinct kernels sharing a label. Omega_third_reading_capital_accumulation identifies a potential third reading (capital accumulation frame) deferred for structural budget.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The shared commitment 'AI poses serious risks requiring governance and resource allocation'
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested between technical AI researchers (citing capability projections, alignment theory) and social scientists/affected communities (citing empirical harm evidence, justice frameworks). Neither has uncontested interpretive authority; the contest IS the system's current state.

readings.commitment: AI risk is primarily existential—misaligned AGI poses extinction-level threat; alignment research is paramount
readings.authority_grounding: technical AI researchers, capability extrapolation models, EA/longtermist philosophy
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set: future humanity (including nonexistent persons). Resource allocation: AGI alignment research, capability controls. Timescale: 10-100 years. Beneficiary: x-risk research institutions, longtermist funders. Suppression: near-term algorithmic justice framed as distraction from existential priority.

readings.commitment: AI risk is primarily near-term harms—deployed systems cause measurable discrimination, displacement, surveillance now; justice interventions are paramount
readings.authority_grounding: social scientists, affected communities, empirical harm documentation, justice/fairness frameworks
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set: present marginalized populations (racialized, low-wage, surveilled). Resource allocation: bias audits, worker protections, surveillance regulation. Timescale: 0-5 years. Beneficiary: marginalized communities, fairness/accountability researchers. Suppression: x-risk framed as speculative distraction from urgent present harms.

axiom_contradictions.basis: Uncertain axiom contradiction status (flagged in omega_hybrid_framework_possibility). The readings hold mutually exclusive VICTIM PRIORITIZATION (future humanity vs present marginalized populations) and compete for zero-sum resources, but it is unclear whether a single coherent framework could hold both as complementary considerations at different timescales. May be licensed plurality (both readings socially live, no single framework required) rather than axiom contradiction (mutual logical exclusion). Requires generation to determine whether the conflict is resource-political or axiom-logical.
